bugs.text: The entry-wave counter advances on entryDone%10 in the middle of the update loop, so 8 group-0 Zako stop one point before their slot and group 2 is skipped; waveIdx only increases, so 16 enemies stay in the 'entry' state forever and fillDone never becomes true.
Zako rows use columns 0-9 but COLS has 8 entries, so 4 Zako get NaN positions. They are invisible and can never be shot.

Because fillDone is never set and 4 enemies cannot be killed, stageState never becomes 'ready': no enemy ever dives, no tractor beam, stage 1 can never be cleared. All dive, capture, dual-fighter and challenging-stage features never run.
csHits is never incremented, so challenging-stage hits and bonuses would always be 0.
Capture sets the player dead without setting respawnT, so the next ship would never spawn (unreachable).
A freed captive has no movement code and could never dock (unreachable).
The hostile captive has no update logic and would block stage clear (unreachable).
A diver returning to its slot teleports; the 'returning' glide state is never assigned.
stageT is never reset, so STAGE N shows only at stage 1 of the first game after page load.
The Boss row sits at y=0 and the first Goei row at y=20, overlapping the 1UP/HIGH SCORE HUD text.
Every stage badge is the same flag labelled '5', including at stage 1.
The enemy-hit sound is defined but never played.

summary: The code is tidy and well organised: a correct fixed-timestep loop, crisp integer scaling, clean pixel-art sprites with wing flaps, a two-hit Boss with a colour change, a proper title screen, a results screen and a localStorage high score. But two layout and sequencing bugs break the game itself. The entry-wave counter leaves 16 enemies in their entry state forever, and 4 Zako get NaN positions from an out-of-range column index. So the formation is never complete, enemies never dive, the tractor beam, capture, dual fighter and challenging stages never run, and stage 1 can never be cleared. In play, you shoot at a static, swaying formation that only fires bullets until you lose your ships, which the play-test confirms. Much of the Galaga-specific code that would run after that point is also incomplete or buggy: captives that don't move, hits that are never counted, a missing respawn after capture. It looks like Galaga, but it is not faithful to it.
